# SK2101 — `[Pure]` is applied to a method that returns nothing

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `void` method carries `System.Diagnostics.Contracts.PureAttribute` or `JetBrains.Annotations.PureAttribute`, neither of which can be true of a method that returns nothing.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| Supersedes | S3603 |

## Why

The two accepted attributes fail for two different reasons and both fail. The BCL's `[Pure]` promises no visible state change; a `void` method that makes no visible state change and returns nothing has no observable effect at all, so either the annotation is wrong or the method is dead. JetBrains' `[Pure]` means the return value must be used; a `void` method has no return value, so the annotation is inapplicable by its own definition. ⚠ The annotation is load-bearing in Skala specifically: `SK2002` reads it to decide whether a discarded result matters, so an annotation that cannot be true feeds a second rule bad input.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
[Pure]
static void Validate(string input) => Check(input);
```

Write:

```csharp
[Pure]
static bool IsValid(string input) => Check(input);
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **There are at least three different `PureAttribute`s and they do not mean the same thing**, so the rule resolves by namespace-qualified name and accepts exactly two: `System.Diagnostics.Contracts.PureAttribute` and `JetBrains.Annotations.PureAttribute`. Anything else spelled `PureAttribute` is declined — a third-party attribute that happens to share the simple name is under no obligation to mean either thing, and matching on the short name is how an annotation rule acquires false positives on code it has never seen. ⚠ **The comparison is a string rather than `Compilation.GetTypeByMetadataName`**, which returns null when two referenced assemblies both declare the name; JetBrains' annotations are routinely present twice, once from the package and once from a source-embedded `Annotations.cs`, and resolving by metadata name would silently answer "not that attribute" in exactly the repositories where the rule has the most to say. ⚠ **A method with an `out` or `ref` parameter is declined even when it returns `void`** — its results leave through the parameters, Code Contracts explicitly permitted that shape, and "returns nothing" is not true of it in the sense the rule means. Only methods and local functions are examined; `[Pure]` also targets a class, a property, an event, a parameter and a delegate, and on those there is no return type to contradict. One finding per declaration rather than one per annotation: two `[Pure]` attributes from two vendors on one `void` method is one mistake. ⚠ **The fix removes every accepted annotation, not only the one the finding points at** — a fix that left the second behind fired the rule again on its own output, which is a `skala fix` loop, and the harness caught that rather than the reasoning doing so. A list every one of whose attributes is being deleted goes as one span, because deleting them individually would leave `[]` behind and an empty attribute list does not parse. Generated code is excluded.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2101.severity`
